original_sample_description: Protocols: Fresh feces of volunteers were collected, frozen and stored in -80芒聞聝 for a few months. The total DNA from every fecal sample was extracted by Magnetic Soil And Stool DNA Kit of TIANGEN BIOTECH (BEIJING) CO., LTD, then constructed into a library and sequenced by Illumina PE150. This process was completed by the Wuhan metware Biotechnology Co., Ltd.There are mainly two methods in QC for DNA samples:(1) DNA degradation degree and potential contamination was monitored on 1%agarose gels. (2) DNA concentration was measured using Qubit脗庐 dsDNA Assay Kit inQubit脗庐 2.0 Flurometer (Life Technologies, CA, USA). OD value is between 1.8~2.0,DNA contents above 1ug are used to constructlibrary. A total amount of 1脦录g DNA per sample was used as input material for the DNA sample preparations. Sequencing libraries were generated using NEBNext脗庐 Ultra芒聞垄 DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB,USA) following manufacturer's recommendations and index codes were added to attribute sequences to each sample. Briefly, the DNA sample was fragmented by sonication to a size of 350bp,then DNA fragments were end-polished, A-tailed, and ligated with the full-length adaptor for Illumina sequencing with further PCR amplification. At last, PCR products were purified (AMPure XP system) and libraries were analysed for size distribution by Agilent2100 Bioanalyzer and quantified using real-timePCR.

The total DNA from every fecal sample was extracted by Magnetic Soil And Stool DNA Kit of TIANGEN BIOTECH (BEIJING) CO., LTD, then constructed into a library and sequenced by Illumina PE150. This process was completed by the Wuhan metware Biotechnology Co., Ltd.There are mainly two methods in QC for DNA samples:(1) DNA degradation degree and potential contamination was monitored on 1%agarose gels. (2) DNA concentration was measured using Qubit脗庐 dsDNA Assay Kit inQubit脗庐 2.0 Flurometer (Life Technologies, CA, USA). OD value is between 1.8~2.0,DNA contents above 1ug are used to constructlibrary. A total amount of 1脦录g DNA per sample was used as input material for the DNA sample preparations. Sequencing libraries were generated using NEBNext脗庐 Ultra芒聞垄 DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB,USA) following manufacturer's recommendations and index codes were added to attribute sequences to each sample. Briefly, the DNA sample was fragmented by sonication to a size of 350bp,then DNA fragments were end-polished, A-tailed, and ligated with the full-length adaptor for Illumina sequencing with further PCR amplification. At last, PCR products were purified (AMPure XP system) and libraries were analysed for size distribution by Agilent2100 Bioanalyzer and quantified using real-timePCR.

original_sample_description: Gut microbiome obesity index, a new analytical part of the metagenomics workflow to evaluate gut dysbiosis in obese humans

Protocols: Fresh feces of volunteers were collected, frozen and stored in -80芒聞聝 for a few months. The total DNA from every fecal sample was extracted by Magnetic Soil And Stool DNA Kit of TIANGEN BIOTECH (BEIJING) CO., LTD, then constructed into a library and sequenced by Illumina PE150. This process was completed by the Wuhan metware Biotechnology Co., Ltd.There are mainly two methods in QC for DNA samples:(1) DNA degradation degree and potential contamination was monitored on 1%agarose gels. (2) DNA concentration was measured using Qubit脗庐 dsDNA Assay Kit inQubit脗庐 2.0 Flurometer (Life Technologies, CA, USA). OD value is between 1.8~2.0,DNA contents above 1ug are used to constructlibrary. A total amount of 1脦录g DNA per sample was used as input material for the DNA sample preparations. Sequencing libraries were generated using NEBNext脗庐 Ultra芒聞垄 DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB,USA) following manufacturer's recommendations and index codes were added to attribute sequences to each sample. Briefly, the DNA sample was fragmented by sonication to a size of 350bp,then DNA fragments were end-polished, A-tailed, and ligated with the full-length adaptor for Illumina sequencing with further PCR amplification. At last, PCR products were purified (AMPure XP system) and libraries were analysed for size distribution by Agilent2100 Bioanalyzer and quantified using real-timePCR.

original_sample_description: Discovery of disease-adapted bacterial lineages in inflammatory bowel diseases

Protocols: Fresh feces of volunteers were collected, frozen and stored in -80芒聞聝 for a few months. The total DNA from every fecal sample was extracted by Magnetic Soil And Stool DNA Kit of TIANGEN BIOTECH (BEIJING) CO., LTD, then constructed into a library and sequenced by Illumina PE150. This process was completed by the Wuhan metware Biotechnology Co., Ltd.There are mainly two methods in QC for DNA samples:(1) DNA degradation degree and potential contamination was monitored on 1%agarose gels. (2) DNA concentration was measured using Qubit脗庐 dsDNA Assay Kit inQubit脗庐 2.0 Flurometer (Life Technologies, CA, USA). OD value is between 1.8~2.0,DNA contents above 1ug are used to constructlibrary. A total amount of 1脦录g DNA per sample was used as input material for the DNA sample preparations. Sequencing libraries were generated using NEBNext脗庐 Ultra芒聞垄 DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB,USA) following manufacturer's recommendations and index codes were added to attribute sequences to each sample. Briefly, the DNA sample was fragmented by sonication to a size of 350bp,then DNA fragments were end-polished, A-tailed, and ligated with the full-length adaptor for Illumina sequencing with further PCR amplification. At last, PCR products were purified (AMPure XP system) and libraries were analysed for size distribution by Agilent2100 Bioanalyzer and quantified using real-timePCR.

original_sample_description: Functional metagenomic selections were performed from various pediatric fecal metagenomes, enriched for children in the first two years of life. A major goal was to understand how antibiotic resistance genes establish and propagate among developing intestinal microbiomes. Fecal metagenomic DNA was cloned into an E. coli library and subjected to selections for antibiotic resistance. Functional metagenomic selections were performed from various pediatric fecal metagenomes, enriched for children in the first two years of life. A major goal was to understand how antibiotic resistance genes establish and propagate among developing intestinal microbiomes. Fecal metagenomic DNA was cloned into an E. coli library and subjected to selections for antibiotic resistance. Functional metagenomic selections were performed from various pediatric fecal metagenomes, enriched for children in the first two years of life. A major goal was to understand how antibiotic resistance genes establish and propagate among developing intestinal microbiomes. Fecal metagenomic DNA was cloned into an E. coli library and subjected to selections for antibiotic resistance. After selection, resistance-conferring fragments (the only fragments conferring survival to E. coli in the presence of the drugs) were PCR-amplified, sequenced, and assembled.

In immunocompromised patients, the influence of microbiological host factors, particularly the patients? gut microbiome on the course of colonization with multi-resistant bacteria like ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-E) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE), is largely unknown. Recent studies indicate that oncological therapy, antibiotic treatment and presence of inflammation lead to a shift in the microbial composition in the gut and, thus, facilitate bloodstream infections and horizontal gene transfer. The present study aims to further elucidate the underlying processes in a longitudinal cohort study of hematological high risk patients.

Fecal metagenomic DNA was cloned into an E. coli library and subjected to selections for antibiotic resistance. In immunocompromised patients, the influence of microbiological host factors, particularly the patients? gut microbiome on the course of colonization with multi-resistant bacteria like ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-E) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE), is largely unknown. Recent studies indicate that oncological therapy, antibiotic treatment and presence of inflammation lead to a shift in the microbial composition in the gut and, thus, facilitate bloodstream infections and horizontal gene transfer. The present study aims to further elucidate the underlying processes in a longitudinal cohort study of hematological high risk patients.

In immunocompromised patients, the influence of microbiological host factors, particularly the patients? gut microbiome on the course of colonization with multi-resistant bacteria like ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-E) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE), is largely unknown. Recent studies indicate that oncological therapy, antibiotic treatment and presence of inflammation lead to a shift in the microbial composition in the gut and, thus, facilitate bloodstream infections and horizontal gene transfer. The present study aims to further elucidate the underlying processes in a longitudinal cohort study of hematological high risk patients.

Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

original_sample_description: Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

original_sample_description: Metagenome or environmental sample from human gut metagenome
Metagenome or environmental sample from human gut metagenome

Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

original_sample_description: gut microbiota from Chilean Children

Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

original_sample_description: Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

Cystic fibrosis (CF), is a lethal hereditary disorder leading to respiratory infections, chronic inflammation, repeated antibiotic treatments, all of them have a known or suspected link to the gut microbiota. The aim of this work was to investigate the gut microbiota composition and modulation of CF patients by metagenomics and metabolomic combined analyses in relation with healthy children. Thirty faecal samples from either CF patients and healthy children (HC) (age range 1-6 years), were collected. After the filtering protocols, a total of 316,006 sequence reads of 16S rRNA gene Amplicons were obtained with an average of 5,356 reads/sample and an average length of 487 bp calculated after primer removal. The results of alpha-diversity analysis indicated a satisfactory coverage of the microbial diversity as shown by the Good¡¯s estimated sample coverage (ESC) that was in all cases above 97%. The sample type (CF vs HC) significantly influenced the composition of the microbiota as measured using ADONIS and ANOSIM methods (p<0.001). Accordingly, beta-diversity analyses performed by unweighted uniFrac showed a clear differentiation between CF and HC individuals suggesting that different taxa characterized the fecal microbiota of the two types of subjects. In fact, Clostridiaceae were more abundant in CF (avg. 20%) compared to HC (avg. 3%) samples (p<0.005) while Ruminococcaceae and Erysipelotrichaceae were more abundant in HC samples (p<0.005). At deeper taxonomic assignment, Clostridium sp. (avg. 9.8% in CF vs 2.2 in HC) and Clostridium difficile (avg. 2.9% in CF vs 0.0 in HC) were more abundant in CF patients (p=0.04 and p=0.01, respectively). By contrast, Eggerthella sp., Eggerthella lenta, Ruminococcus sp., Ruminococcus bromii, Dialister sp. and Dialister invisus were more abundant in HC feces (p<0.05).

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

The present study attempts to catalogue the taxonomic diversity of gut microbiomes sampled from an urban cohort from Ahmedabad city in Western India. The uploaded sequence data corresponds to 160 stool samples collected from 80 healthy individuals at two time-points, 60 days apart.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

Gut lumen microbiota from individual 18  male  BMI<25

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

HMB-IRB-NPU

The present study attempts to catalogue the taxonomic diversity of gut microbiomes sampled from an urban cohort from Ahmedabad city in Western India. The uploaded sequence data corresponds to 160 stool samples collected from 80 healthy individuals at two time-points, 60 days apart.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

Gut lumen microbiota from individual 36  female  BMI<25

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.

We performed computational and experimental analysis of healthy human fecal samples to examine the TLR4 signaling capacity of the gut microbiota. This analysis revealed that an immuno-inhibitory activity of LPS, conserved across the Bacteroidales and derived from an under-acylated structural feature, silences TLR4 signaling for the entire consortium of organisms inhabiting the human gut. Comparative analysis of metagenomic data from the Human Microbiome Project and healthy donor samples indicates that immune silencing via LPS is a microbe intrinsic feature in all healthy adults.
